name: Manas National Park & Tiger Reserve
description: An UNESCO World Heritage Site, Biosphere Reserve, and Project Tiger reserve sprawling across 950 square kilometers in the Himalayan foothills along the crystal-clear Manas River on the international border with Bhutan.

name: Haflong
description: Haflong, situated in the Dima Hasao district of Assam, is a treasure trove of natural beauty and adventure. With its rolling hills, sparkling waterfalls, and lush green forests, Haflong is a haven for trekking enthusiasts and nature lovers. The town is surrounded by the Borail range, which offers breathtaking views and exciting trekking trails. Haflong's unique culture is a blend of Assamese and Dimasa traditions, making it a fascinating destination for those interested in exploring the region's rich heritage. As a popular trekking destination, Haflong offers a range of outdoor activities, including rock climbing, bird watching, and camping, making it an ideal getaway for adventure seekers.

name: Umrangso
description: Perched in the verdant expanse of Dima Hasao district in Assam, Umrangso presents an otherworldly trekking experience for the bold and the intrepid. A treasure trove of rich biodiversity, the region boasts a mesmerizing mix of tropical rainforests, rolling hills, and crystal-clear waterfalls. For those seeking an adrenaline rush, Umrangso offers an array of adventure activities, all nestled amidst the grandeur of the Himalayan foothills. Whether you're a seasoned trekker or a nature enthusiast, Umrangso promises to leave you enchanted and rejuvenated.

name: Naranarayan Setu

name: Kaziranga National Park
description: Spanning 858 square kilometers in the Brahmaputra floodplains, an UNESCO World Heritage site and Tiger Reserve hosting two-thirds of the world's Great One-Horned Rhinoceroses, along with wild water buffaloes, swamp deer, and royal Bengal tigers.

name: Hajo
description: Hajo, a picturesque village in Assam, is a treasure trove of natural beauty, rich history, and spiritual significance. This ancient pilgrimage site is nestled on the banks of the Brahmaputra River and is home to numerous temples, most notably the Hayagriva Madhav Temple, which attracts devotees from all over the country. The region's unique cultural landscape is a fascinating blend of Hindu, Buddhist, and Islamic influences, reflected in its architectural heritage and traditional practices. As visitors wander through the village, they can immerse themselves in the tranquility of the surroundings, explore the historic temples, and engage with the warm and hospitable local community.

name: Sualkuchi

name: Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary

name: Sibsagar
description: Sibsagar, situated in the heart of Assam, is a treasure trove of natural beauty, rich history, and diverse culture. This ancient town, once the capital of the Ahom kingdom, boasts an array of majestic lakes, including the iconic Joysagar Lake, which is one of the largest man-made lakes in the country. The town's landscape is dotted with numerous archaeological sites, temples, and monuments, showcasing the region's architectural and cultural heritage. As a trekker's haven, Sibsagar offers endless opportunities to explore its lush forests, tea gardens, and rolling hills, providing a unique blend of adventure, nature, and serenity. The region is also a birdwatcher's paradise, with over 200 species of birds, including the iconic Greater Adjutant Stork and the Lesser Adjutant Stork.

name: Tezpur

The town's unique blend of natural beauty, historical significance, and cultural richness makes it a must-visit destination for anyone looking to explore the authentic essence of Assam.

name: Dibru-Saikhowa National Park
description: Located in northeastern Assam, Dibru-Saikhowa National Park is a 340-square-kilometer protected area that offers a glimpse into the region's rich biodiversity. This national park, which was declared a wildlife sanctuary in 1986 and a national park in 1997, serves as a vital habitat for the rare and endangered greater adjutant stork and Bengal florican. The park's diverse landscape, comprising wetlands, grasslands, and tropical forests, makes it an ideal destination for nature walks, bird watching, and photography.
